What SQL injection is (high-level)
SQL injection happens when a web application improperly includes user input in a database query. If the input isn’t safely handled, an attacker can manipulate the query’s logic to access or modify data they shouldn’t.
Common causes
Concatenating raw user input directly into SQL queries
Lack of input validation/sanitization
Overly permissive database privileges
Poor error handling that reveals database details
How to prevent it
Use parameterized queries (prepared statements)
— this is the most important fix
Use ORM frameworks
that automatically handle query safety
Validate and sanitize inputs
(e.g., allowlists, type checks)
Apply least-privilege access
to database accounts
Use stored procedures safely
(without dynamic SQL inside them)
Escape inputs only as a secondary measure
, not the main defense
Implement web application firewalls (WAFs)
for additional protection
Monitor and log suspicious activity

Unsafe (vulnerable):

*

users

username
